title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — all sinners because all die; not from latent corruption
pass_a_gloss: Add: Paul proves here that all humans are sinners—sin in the world, that is, in humans—by this argument, that all die. Do you think he proves sin is in humans because hereditary corruption is in humans—the very thing to be proved? Does he argue from a latent moral corruption when the open, known death of all was at hand?
pass_b_english: Add that the Apostle proves in this place that all humans are sinners, that sin is in the world, that is in humans, by this argument, that all die. Do you think he proves that sin is in humans, because there is sin in humans, namely hereditary corruption? Does he draw the argument from a latent moral corruption, which itself was to be proved, when it was at hand from the open and known death of all?
source_text: Adde quod Apostolus probat hoc loco omnes homines esse peccatores, peccatum in mundo, id est in hominibus, hoc argumento, quod omnes moriuntur. Putasne probare eum peccatum esse in hominibus, quia sit in hominibus peccatum, nimirum corruptio haereditaria? Num a latente corruptione morali, quae ipsa erat probanda, ducit argumentum, cum suppeteret a patente & nota omnium morte?
